paper.title: Emergence of scaling in random networks

headline: Barabasi-Albert 1999 (mildly agent-based): 1/3 locked clauses REPRO; gamma_mle(m=3)=2.681 (kmin=m+1, discrete MLE); BA/ER max-degree ratio=17.7x

verdicts.gate: P1 fitted gamma(m=3) in [2.7, 3.3] (power-law tail, gamma~3)
P3 BA max degree >= 3x ER max degree at equal mean degree (hubs)

extra.fit_method: discrete CSN-2009 MLE, kmin=m+1 (graded); CCDF slope (secondary)
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; mildly agent-based (arriving NodeAgents make a preferential-attachment decision); the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce the scale-free exponent and would catch a tuned fit

citations: Barabasi, A.-L. & Albert, R. (1999). Emergence of scaling in random networks. Science 286(5439):509-512. doi:10.1126/science.286.5439.509.
Clauset, A., Shalizi, C.R. & Newman, M.E.J. (2009). Power-law distributions in empirical data. SIAM Review 51(4):661-703. doi:10.1137/070710111 (discrete MLE estimator, eq. 3.5).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction. Sanity cross-check (not graded): networkx.barabasi_albert_graph under the same fit yields gamma within ~0.02 of this generator, confirming the exponent is a property of the model+fit, not a generator bug
